transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood), Marco Alvarez (Redwood), Sofia Patel (Lumina), Dr. Ben Larson (Lumina), Priya Nair (Lumina)

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, welcome, this is Avery from Redwood, thanks so much for joining our little podcast chat today. Um, we've got a few questions we want to run through - nothing super formal - just want to capture the story of how Lumina's using Redwood.

[00:14] Sofia: Thanks, Avery, excited to be here. Ben and Priya are with me, excited to share a bit.

[00:21] Marco: Hey all - quick housekeeping, we'll record audio and share draft copy after the call. If anything needs to be redacted let us know.

[00:33] Dr. Ben: Sounds good.

[00:36] Avery: Great. First question for Sofia: at a high level, what was the business problem you were trying to solve with LLMs, and what led you to Redwood?

[00:48] Sofia: Yeah, so for Lumina, it was about patient support and triage - we wanted richer conversational guidance in our care pathways, but we needed it to be predictable, low latency, and compliant with health regs. We had tried a couple of hosted APIs, but the latency variability and the costs at scale were the big unknowns. Redwood came up in a few vendor reviews - we liked the idea of dedicated pools and the clear tooling for observability.

[01:12] Priya: And from the eng side, we needed a drop-in that could replace our quirky mix of microservices without changing too much of the app logic. The Redwood SDK and the model catalog made the integration less painful.

[01:27] Avery: Nice - Ben, any technical surprises during rollout?

[01:31] Dr. Ben: A few. First, the KV cash - sorry, KV cache - handling was a little different than our in-house cache, so we had to adjust cache keys for session affinity. There were some initial bumps with sequence lengths, our prompts were long and we had to optimize truncation logic. But Redwood's SEs helped run a quick perf sweep and suggested a quantization profile that saved a lot on cost without noticeable quality impact.

[01:58] Marco: Can you give a ballpark on the cost improvement? I know these numbers are sensitive so a rough percent is fine.

[02:06] Priya: Sure - we saw roughly a 30% reduction in per-token cost after moving to dedicated capacity and applying the batching and quantization suggestions. For high-volume flows, that translated into a meaningful monthly savings.

[02:21] Sofia: And latency improved too; our median token latency dropped from ~220ms to around 95-110ms for the common paths - which made the UI feel much snappier for clinicians using the tool.

[02:36] Avery: That's great, and obviously nice for adoption. Were there any security or compliance concerns that required special handling?

[02:44] Sofia: Yes - we had to ensure audit logs and encryption at rest. Redwood's private option and KMS integrations were important during procurement. We ended up doing a private deployment in our VPC with customer-managed keys, which satisfied the security team.

[03:02] Dr. Ben: There was also an internal review around data residency, but Redwood's region routing and data retention controls gave us enough confidence.

[03:12] Marco: On the technical side, Priya, did you run any benchmarks or regressions you can share for the case study?

[03:19] Priya: We ran synthetic load tests and a small canary in production. I can share a short table in the follow-up, but high-level: throughput scaled linearly up to our expected concurrency, and fallbacks worked as advertised during a simulated outage where Redwood routed to a lower-cost variant gracefully.

[03:41] Avery: Love the 'graceful fallback' story - that'll be great in the copy. Any memorable stakeholder feedback or a quote we should try to capture?

[03:50] Sofia: Yeah - clinicians called it 'instant context' in early feedback; that's probably a good quote - maybe: 'Redwood made our triage suggestions feel like a colleague, not a black box.'

[04:04] Marco: Perfect. Ben, any little engineering anecdote - maybe something fun for the audience?

[04:09] Dr. Ben: We had an early test where the model hallucinated a really bizarre medication name, which of course triggered laughter in the review meeting. The safety filters and prompt templates helped reduce that. It's a reminder that evals are still crucial.

[04:26] Priya: Yeah, and we set up eval suites keyed to common clinical scenarios so we could catch regressions during model rollouts. Redwood's rollback policies were handy for quick remediation.

[04:39] Avery: Great specifics - we'll weave that in. Any competitive diligence - were you evaluating other vendors?

[04:46] Sofia: We did look at OpenAI's hosted endpoints and Anthropic for safety work, and a couple of self-hosted runtimes. Ultimately Redwood's combination of dedicated pools, observability, and private deployment options won out.

[04:59] Marco: Quick question about metrics - do you mind if we include the 30% cost savings and the latency numbers in the case study headline?

[05:09] Sofia: That's fine, as long as you include a short note that these are approximate and representative for our high-volume flows. We'll sign off on the exact wording.

[05:18] Avery: Sounds good. Logistics: we plan to send a draft case study and a 60s highlight clip. We also might need legal to lightly review the quote.

[05:27] Sofia: Yep - our legal team will want to see the final copy, but we're comfortable with the high-level numbers and the quote.

[05:34] Marco: Anything else technically that you'd like us to call out? For instance, the quantization profile or the batching config?

[05:41] Priya: You can mention quantization and batching in the technical sidebar - maybe call out that we used the Redwood's "Opt-quant small" profile - I'm not sure of the exact name, maybe the team will confirm - it's okay if that gets a little garbled in the transcript.

[05:58] Dr. Ben: Also the SDK made retry logic and distributed tracing straightforward to hook into our observability stack, that was surprisingly simple.

[06:07] Avery: Nice. Wrapping up - any final thoughts?

[06:10] Sofia: We're excited to keep working with Redwood; it's helped us get from prototype to scaling faster than expected.

[06:16] Priya: And for engineering teams thinking about this, plan for prompt length and evals early.

[06:21] Marco: Awesome. We'll circulate the draft copy and the audio. Thanks everyone for your time.

[06:27] Dr. Ben: Thanks - looking forward to the final edit.

[06:30] Avery: Thanks so much. End recording.

Notes:
- Some transcription artifacts: 'KV cash' appears where 'KV cache' is meant; 'Redwood Opti-quant' referenced loosely.
- Shared artifacts: Avery will attach the draft case study, an asset pack (logo/headshots), and the highlight clip link in follow-up.

End of transcript.
